request: Make ordering feel slick, with nice animations and transitions between the steps. It belongs under Feature #40 (Online ordering).

exchanges.say: You want ordering to feel slick, with nice animations and transitions. I read "slick" and "nice" as feelings and "animations" and "transitions" as motion we still have to pin down. Today the only motion is a 150 ms button fade (motion:web/styles/buttons.css), nothing honours reduced motion (gap:reduced-motion), and the order flow is five steps (flow:/order). Four questions, riskiest first.

questions.ask: Which moments should move? Today the only motion is the buttons' 150 ms fade (motion:web/styles/buttons.css), and the order flow is five steps (flow:/order). I'd start with moving between steps and adding to the basket. OK?
questions.default: Moving between steps and adding an item, because motion that explains a change the customer caused is the kind that does not get redone.

questions.ask: Is "slick" and "nice" only about motion, or also about changing the steps themselves?
questions.default: Only motion; the steps stay as they are.

questions.ask: Within a step change, what moves and what stays still? The Stepper and BasketSummary are shared components.
questions.default: Only the step content moves; shared chrome stays put so the page does not feel like it jumps.

questions.ask: Nothing in the app honours prefers-reduced-motion yet (gap:reduced-motion). With reduced motion on, should the motion go entirely?
questions.default: No movement at all with reduced motion on, because motion can make some people unwell.

answers.text: Two moments: moving between the order steps, and an item going into the basket. Nothing else needs to move.
Slick and nice just mean the motion for me; don't change anything else about the steps.
The step content slides in the direction you are going; the header and the basket summary stay still. The basket count gives a small pop when an item goes in.
With reduced motion on, nothing slides or pops; the step and the count just change at once.

exchanges.say: So: two moments, only the step content and the basket count move, and nothing moves with reduced motion on. Now the numbers and the proof.

questions.ask: How long may each motion take? Your buttons already use 150 ms. I'd propose 200 ms for a step change and 150 ms for the basket. Your numbers?
questions.default: 200 ms and 150 ms, as proposals for you to confirm.
ease-out, to match the existing fade.

questions.ask: How do we prove it: a recording of each moment with reduced motion off and on?
And a check over the changed styles that every duration is one you confirmed?
questions.default: Yes: a metric over the changed style files.

questions.ask: Should it hold a frame rate on a mid-range phone?
questions.default: Only transform and opacity animated; no frame-rate number unless you have one.

answers.text: Keep it quick: step changes in 200 ms, and the basket pop in 150 ms, like the buttons already fade.
A recording of both moments, once with reduced motion off and once with it on.
Don't worry about frame rates for this one.

exchanges.say: Nearly done. One idea of mine you can say no to.

questions.ask: An idea: a small celebration animation on the order confirmation. Want it?

answers.text: That is not part of what I asked for; park it.

exchanges.say: Here is what done looks like. Goal: moving through the order steps and adding a loaf feel responsive, so customers can tell where they are. Done when: moving between steps slides the step content over 200 ms while the header and basket summary stay still; adding a loaf pops the basket count over 150 ms; with reduced motion on, both change at once with no movement; and every duration in the changed styles is 150 or 200 ms. Checkpoints: first the step slide, then the basket pop, then reduced motion and the duration check. Easing is ease-out (your accepted default); frame rates and the confirmation animation are parked.
